# ADR-029: One daily digest with an audio overview, generated by Gemini

**Status:** Accepted · 2026-11-17 · adds `digest` job kind, schema v7

## Context

A reader who follows many blogs gets every post one by one and no overview of the day. The owner asked
for the opposite: pick RSS/blog sources, pick a language (English or Tamil) and an hour; once a day,
one rich message with an audio player and a numbered summary of every post received in the last 24 h.

The bot had no model and no voice. It did have: a SQLite job queue with priorities and a retry ladder,
DST-safe wall-clock slot arithmetic, Readability + Telegra.ph (ADR-007), the media downloader with its
SSRF and size gates (ADR-012/028), the rich-message renderer and sender (ADR-023/025), and `ffmpeg` in
the image.

Four questions decided the shape:

| Question | Decision |
|---|---|
| Provider | Gemini for both halves: one `GEMINI_API_KEY`, text and speech (`gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.8-flash-tts`), over plain `fetch` |
| Per-post delivery | Unchanged. The digest is **extra**; a selected source keeps delivering one by one |
| Destination | Any chat the user already delivers to, one digest per chat |
| Busy days | Every post is summarised; the message splits into Part 1, Part 2… |

## Options

| Option | Result | Cost | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. A `digest` job in the existing queue** | retries, backoff, priorities and the Telegram rate limiter come for free | one new job kind and one case in the worker | **Chosen** |
| B. A separate digest service or cron container | independent schedule | a second process, a second database writer, and a second copy of the queue — breaks ADR-002 | Rejected |
| C. Summarise at fetch time, only voice at digest time | faster digest runs | every post pays Gemini, including the ones whose source is never in a digest, and a language change invalidates everything | Rejected: cost without a user |
| D. A second provider for the voice (Azure) | better Tamil timbre | two keys, two bills, two failure modes for one feature | Rejected for now: one key was the requirement |

## Decision

- **The window tiles; it is not "the last 24 h from now".** A run checks its sources once (the
  manual-check path, so no `next_slot_at` moves), then pins `window_end` and selects
  `first_seen_at >= max(last_window_end ?? 0, window_end − 24 h) AND first_seen_at < window_end`,
  newest first. After the last part is sent, one statement sets `last_window_end = window_end` and
  clears the pin. A retry reuses the pin, so it selects the posts the failed attempt selected; two
  consecutive digests never show the same post; nothing older than a day is ever selected.
- **The pin is one instant after the source check.** The check records what it finds with the run's
  clock, and the window's upper bound is strict, so pinning at that same instant would push every
  just-found post into tomorrow's digest. A pin older than a day (only a run that died can leave one)
  is dropped, so it cannot hold back the next day's posts, and switching the digest off clears the pin.
  The commit writes the run's own `window_end` value rather than re-reading the row, so a toggle during
  a run cannot turn `last_window_end` into NULL and re-send a day.
- **The time is an hour (0-23) in the owner's zone.** `digestSlot` reuses the source slots'
  wall-clock arithmetic (`wallToUtc`), so a DST change moves the digest with the clock. Enabling or
  changing the hour writes `next_run_at`; disabling sets it to NULL. The tick advances every due slot
  **before** enqueueing (§4.2) and skips a slot older than `LATE_SLOT_MS`.
- **No key, no feature.** `GEMINI_API_KEY` unset makes `cfg.digest` undefined: the S1 button is not
  rendered and the tick passes `digests: false`, so no job is ever queued.
- **Each role walks a model ladder.** Quotas and capacity are per model, so a 429/5xx (or an answer
  with nothing usable in it) moves summaries and the script to the next text model and the voice to
  the next TTS model. The order is the free tier's own rate table, latest to oldest, and a ledger in
  `gemini_quota` skips a rung whose day or minute is spent instead of earning a 429 (ADR-033): the
  current ladders live in `src/config.ts` and in `.env.example`. A network error or an abort ends the
  ladder at once; every step is logged (`gemini_model_fallback`, `gemini_rung_spent`). Both tails are
  config (`GEMINI_TEXT_FALLBACKS`, `GEMINI_TTS_FALLBACKS`).
  The two legacy TTS previews predate the interactions audio format: they speak through
  `models/{id}:generateContent` with the AUDIO modality and return raw L16 PCM, which joins the same
  chunks. The Live models are not part of it: they speak only over the Live API's stateful WebSocket,
  not the unary interactions call, and Google positions them for conversation, not recitation.
- **Per-post summaries are cached by `(post_id, lang)`.** A retry, a second part or a Tamil run after
  an English one never pays twice for the same text. The cache holds the summary and the Telegraph URL;
  the pictures are downloaded per run, because files do not outlive a job.
- **The article is the Telegraph path.** `extractArticle` (Readability) gives the text and the page's
  pictures; `publishArticle` gives the "Read full article" link. A thin page or a failed fetch falls
  back to the feed's own words, and the item still ships.
- **Article pictures are asked for politely:** with the page as `referer` and a browser user-agent.
  Hotlink-protected CDNs (TechCrunch's among them) answer 403 to the extractor's bot agent; with the
  two headers the same URL downloads, verified live. A picture still failing only costs that picture.
- **Pictures live in a per-post folder, and one failed picture costs that picture.** Three summaries
  download at once and the downloader names files by index, so a shared work folder could let one
  post's picture land on another's item; each post downloads into `post-<id>/` and the renderer reads
  each item's own list. Each of the up-to-three URLs is fetched on its own, so a hotlink 403 on one
  never empties the item.
- **The Instant View copy is the page that gets read.** When a post has a page — stored by delivery or
  by an earlier digest — the digest extracts that page instead of the site: static HTML, no paywall,
  no JavaScript. Verified live: 4 140 and 2 936 readable characters with titles intact, and each
  page's figures keep the original CDN URLs — which is why a picture's referer stays the post's own
  page, not the Telegraph one. A dead page (404) falls back to the post itself. Delivery does the
  same on a retry (`planArticle`), and `withReadMore` reuses the stored page instead of writing a
  second one.
- **The model's output is untrusted.** `cleanSummary` flattens every string, drops empty ones and
  clamps headline 120 / description 600 / point 240 / six points; the renderer escapes everything and
  only our own Telegraph link is an anchor (`skip_entity_detection` is already on). A summary with no
  headline or description is no summary, and falls back to the feed.
- **One retry per summary, then the fallback.** If *every* item fell back, Gemini itself is down: the
  run throws `E_FEED_DOWN`, the worker reschedules on the existing ladder, and the pinned window makes
  the retry select the same posts. The fallback is never cached.
- **The script is written from the summaries**, never from the articles, so the audio and the message
  say the same thing: an opening sentence with the date and the count, one paragraph per story, a
  sign-off. Word budget `min(80 + 45 × items, 1400)`.
- **The voice is chunked.** The TTS model takes 8 192 input tokens, so the script is split on
  paragraph → sentence → word boundaries, each piece requested as raw PCM (`audio/l16`, 24 kHz,
  mono). The pieces concatenate, and `ffmpeg` writes one 64 kbps MP3 with the digest's title in its own
  tags. Duration is `PCM bytes / 48 000`. The encode runs `atempo=1.1`, so the same words play 10%
  faster (no pitch shift) and a fixed-length script fits more of the day; the reported duration is
  scaled to match. ADR-033 measured the ceiling: 3 929 Tamil characters came back as 260 s of PCM in
  31 s, while 9 169 failed at the transport level, so a piece is 5 000 characters and a refused piece
  is retried once at 2 500 — the size this ADR originally shipped.
- **The message splits under the Bot API caps.** Greedy in digest order, a part closes before an item
  would pass 49 media (the audio takes the 50th slot in Part 1), 30 000 characters or 480 blocks —
  under 50 / 32 768 / 500. ADR-033 measured what the cap counts: 33 000 characters answer
  `RICH_MESSAGE_TEXT_TOO_LONG`, 24 000 Tamil characters (64 kB of UTF-8) pass, so the budget counts
  the visible text, not the markup, and the one piece whose size the clamps do not bound — the "Also
  today" list — is emitted in chunks a part can always hold. Numbering continues across parts; the
  player is Part 1's; the footer is the last part's. Posts past `DIGEST_MAX_POSTS` are numbered
  headline links under "Also today" instead of being summarised: a cost guard on the model, not a
  summary. Every one of them links to its own Telegraph page, published from the extracted article
  with no model call, so the section reads like the items above; a story whose page cannot be read or
  published keeps its original URL, and a story skipped because the job budget is spent does too. The
  cap defaults to 20 for production; a local run sets `DIGEST_MAX_POSTS=2`. Twenty summarised posts
  with their pictures exceed one message, so the split above lands them in two balanced parts.
- **The read-full link is a label, not a URL.** Each item ends with
  `<a href="telegraph">📖 Read full article</a>`; the raw address never appears as visible text.
- **One budget for the whole job.** `DIGEST_BUDGET_MS = 8 min` aborts every network step, because a
  run that outlived `STALE_LOCK_MS` (10 min) could be handed to a second worker. Gemini calls run
  three at a time. If the budget is gone before the message is built, the run throws and retries on
  the pinned window instead of shipping a half-planned digest. Inside that budget each call has its
  own 120 s cap; the cap is a model failure, not a job failure, so a hung model walks the ladder
  while the caller's own abort (the budget) stays fatal. Verified live: the primary voice hung past
  the cap and the digest had no audio until the cap was made to fall through.
- **A running job keeps its claim alive.** The worker now refreshes `locked_at` every minute
  (`queue.touch`), so a long run — a digest over many sources, or any slow job — is never mistaken for
  a crashed one and re-claimed. `recoverStale` then only reclaims jobs whose process really died, which
  is what the `shortcut:` on resend-on-retry assumes.
- **The digest is extra.** No existing user's delivery changes: the job only reads `posts`, never
  marks a delivery, and the sources keep fetching on their own slots.
- **Delivery publishes the Instant View page first; the digest reuses it.** `planArticle` (articles)
  and `withReadMore` (long captions) hand the page they just published to the caller, which stores it
  in `posts.telegraph_url` (schema v7). `summarisePost` and the overflow path read that column before
  asking Telegra.ph again, so a digest over posts the bot already delivered makes no new page
  requests — the flood control only appears for posts nobody published yet. When the digest has to
  publish one itself, it stores that page on the post too, and the column is kept for the life of the
  post (retention prunes posts): a retry, the other language or another user on the same source reads
  the same page instead of writing a second one. A summary row written before v7 can carry a page the
  post row does not — the digest mirrors it down, so delivery reuses it too.
- **The digest's labels stay English in every language.** Only the content translates — Tamil
  headline, description, key points and audio. The heading, date line, audio line, key-points and
  read-full labels, "Also today", the part label and the footer are identical in `en` and `ta`; the
  message's date is formatted `en-GB` in both. The footer is `<b><i>By FeedBerry Bot</i></b>`; the
  "AI-generated summary" sentence and its post count are gone.
- **Tamil mode** writes headline, description, key points and audio in simple spoken Tamil, keeps
  names/brands/technical terms in English, and prints the original title in italics under the
  headline. The rule names the script: every Tamil word in Tamil letters, never romanised. ADR-033
  added the check behind it — a summary with no Tamil script at all (Tanglish) or an English summary
  carrying Tamil is asked again up to twice and then ships as written, never dropped. Screens follow
  the interface language; the message's own labels do not (see above).
- **Every `dg:*` handler authorises.** The digest must belong to the tapper, and a subscription must
  be one of the tapper's own RSS rows; the repo enforces both in `toggleDigestSource`. A refused tap
  writes nothing and paints nothing.

## Consequences

- A digest run costs about one Gemini text call per post plus two calls for the script and the voice
  chunks; the cache makes a retry nearly free. `DIGEST_MAX_POSTS` is the ceiling.
- The window is pinned at the *run* instant, not the scheduled hour, so a late run covers
  `[previous end, now)` and stays contiguous. A slot older than 12 h is skipped, so a bot off for a
  day resumes with one digest rather than two.
- `shortcut:` a crash after some parts were sent resends the whole digest on retry; there is no
  per-part ledger. Upgrade when a duplicate is seen.
- `shortcut:` the digest is English/Tamil only, the voice is fixed (`Kore`), the reason the audio
  failed is only logged, and `DIGEST_MAX_POSTS` silently trades summaries for headline links.
- A digest with no posts still sends the one-line message and commits the window, so an empty day is
  acknowledged exactly once.
- Removing the last source from an enabled digest switches it off, so nobody receives "no new posts"
  every day with no way to tell why.
- A free-tier Gemini key allows 5–15 requests a minute per model and 10–500 requests **per day**
  depending on the rung; a busy day spends the narrow rungs first and the ladder carries the digest
  to the wide ones. The ledger in ADR-033 makes that a decision instead of a 429, and keeps the last
  slots of every rung for the spoken script. When every rung is spent the digest waits on the
  rate-limit ladder (30 min → 8 h). A paid tier removes the limits; the caps are a table in
  `src/config.ts`.

## Evidence

- `npm run typecheck`: exit 0.
- `npm test`: **478/478 pass**, including the eight new files — `digest-render` (English and Tamil
  layouts, 0/1/3 images, escaping, no-audio line, empty window, media/text/block splits, "Also today"),
  `digest-window` (`digestSlot` across both 2026 Berlin DST changes, two runs tiling with no overlap,
  the 24 h clamp over a stale `last_window_end`, and a day-old pin being dropped), `digest-audio`
  (chunk sizes, word integrity, Tamil, duration, a failed voice returning null, and the real ffmpeg
  encode where the host has it), `digest-summary` (clamps, empty strings, cache hit with zero Gemini
  calls, per-language cache, the two-attempt fallback, and the referer/user-agent headers a
  hotlink-protected CDN needs, and two posts with the same picture filename landing in two
  folders), `digest-job` (tick → job → one
  `sendRichMessage` with `tg://audio`, the numbered items, the window committed; a post stamped at the
  run instant is in *this* digest; the two-summary cap leaving the third story under "Also today",
  first with the post URL and then, with a readable page, its Telegraph URL while a second overflow
  story gets its own page too; a 429 on both primaries carried by the
  ladder so the digest still ships with its voice; the empty-window message; every summary failing
  leaves the window pinned and the job queued), `job-lock` (a running claim is refreshed, a finished one is not),
  `digest-gemini` (a 429/5xx or an unusable answer moves the summary, script or voice to the next
  model; an abort never does; a repeated fallback is not called twice; the per-call cap is a model
  failure and the voice moves on; a legacy voice speaks through
  `generateContent`, its WAV container is stripped to PCM, and a rate-limited legacy voice falls to
  the next model), and
  `digest-menu` (button hidden without a key; sources/language/time/on-off; a foreign digest and a
  foreign subscription refused; "on" without a source stays off; removing the last source switches
  the digest off), `telegraph-flood` (a page answered `FLOOD_WAIT_n` is retried after the wait
  the API names; four floods in a row give up and throw), `article-plan` (the page a delivered
  article gets is handed to the caller; a thin page caches nothing), and the delivery/digest pairs
  that carry the cache (`m5` asserts `posts.telegraph_url` after a caption publish; `digest-job`
  reuses a stored link for a summary and for an overflow story with a client that must not publish,
  then finds both columns NULL; `digest-summary` reads the Instant View copy about the seeded link, a
  dead page falls back to the post, and one failed picture leaves the other two; a cached summary
  still downloads its picture with zero Gemini calls; a page the digest publishes is stored on the
  post and written once; the page's own figures lead the three pictures).
- `npm run build`: exit 0, `dist/digest/*.js` written.
- `docker compose build bot`: exit 0, image `daily-digest-bot:latest` built with the new `schema.sql`.
- The deployed artifact, on a fresh volume, against a stand-in Bot API: the container logged
  `{"level":"info","code":"boot","schema":6,…}` and then `polling_started`, and inside it
  `PRAGMA user_version` read `6` with `digest_sources, digests, post_summaries` present.
- **Live**, a throwaway bot (`feedberrytestbot`) and real Gemini: two BBC News / TechCrunch sources
  fetched 41 items, the digest summarised the 2 newest and listed the rest, and Telegram accepted the
  rich message with the uploaded MP3 — English `{"code":"digest_sent","posts":42,"parts":1,"audioSec":68}`
  and Tamil `{"code":"digest_sent","posts":42,"parts":1,"audioSec":61}`. The cache then held, per
  post, an `en` row and a `ta` row — the Tamil headlines in Tamil script with the brands in English
  ("Las Vegas-இல் Uber app வழியாக Zoox robotaxi சேவை அறிமுகம்") — and every row carried its Telegraph URL.
  `gemini-3.8-flash` answered 503/429 at check time, so the live runs named `gemini-3.6-flash`; model
  ids are config and the default is unchanged. Neither direct run carried a picture: the article CDN
  answered 403 to the extractor's bot agent. With the page as `referer` and a browser user-agent the
  same URL downloads, and a run through the real `src/main.ts` (polling → tick → queue → digest) then
  sent `{"code":"digest_sent","posts":42,"parts":1,"images":3,"audioSec":83}` — three article photos
  riding in the slideshow beside the player. The same scheduled path in Tamil, with its summaries
  regenerated, sent `{"code":"digest_sent","posts":42,"parts":1,"images":3,"audioSec":102}` and the
  cache then held three Tamil headlines ("Dreamteam $53M நிதி திரட்டியது: AI-native CRM சந்தையில் புதிய
  போட்டி") with the brands in English.
- The ladder, live: `gemini-3.8-flash` was both rate-limited for the day (`429 … 20 requests per day`)
  and 503, so four `gemini_model_fallback` lines moved the three summaries and the script to
  `gemini-3.6-flash`, and the digest still sent
  `{"code":"digest_sent","posts":43,"parts":1,"images":2,"audioSec":93}`.
- The audio artifact, through `audioOverview` with the real voice: `{"seconds":9,"bytes":69603,
  "codec":"mp3","sampleRate":"24000","channels":1,"containerDuration":"8.593958",
  "title":"FeedBerry digest check","meanVolumeDb":"-18.2","maxVolumeDb":"-2.1"}` — a decodable,
  non-silent MP3 with the digest's title in its own tags (ffprobe + volumedetect), 8.59 s against the
  9.36 s the same words took before `atempo=1.1`. The same run logged the voice fallback:
  `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` answered 503 and `gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts` spoke.
- Both legacy voices, end to end through `audioOverview` (generateContent → L16 PCM → atempo → MP3):
  `gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview` → 8.597 s, mean −16.7 dB; `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` → 8.966 s,
  mean −19.6 dB; both 24 kHz mono MP3 with the ID3 title.
- The final code, live through `src/main.ts` (polling → tick → queue → digest):
  `{"code":"digest_sent","posts":44,"parts":1,"images":4,"audioSec":79}`. That run also showed the
  per-call ceiling working — one summary was aborted at 120 s (`This operation was aborted`) and its
  retry completed — and the daily-capped 3.8 rung handing every text call to `gemini-3.6-flash`.
- After the overflow-link, per-post-folder and two-summary-cap change: `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`
  and `npm run build` re-ran green (464/464 at that point).
- The same code, live, with the local cap (`DIGEST_MAX_POSTS=2`) over a 46-post window:
  `{"code":"digest_sent","posts":46,"parts":1,"images":0,"audioSec":60}`, Telegram answering
  `{"delivered":[2199]}`. Every overflow story got its own page: **44 `digest_page` lines, 0
  failures**, after the client absorbed 13 `FLOOD_WAIT_n` answers with the wait Telegra.ph names
  (`telegraph_flood_wait`). Before the flood retry the same run left 24 of 44 pages unpublished, and
  before the page cap was lifted only the first two overflow stories had a page.
- The reuse cache, live (schema v7 on the same file): two posts were given the pages delivery had
  already published; a Tamil digest over a 47-post window (2 summaries, 45 overflow) then logged
  **43 `digest_page` lines, 0 failures, 13 waits** — exactly the 45 uncached stories — and sent
  `{"code":"digest_sent","posts":47,"parts":1,"images":2,"audioSec":74}`, Telegram answering
  `{"delivered":[2201]}`.
- Stored links survive the send and are never rewritten (the rule this ADR now rests on): a 47-post
  run from an empty cache sent `{"posts":47,"images":3,"audioSec":61}` (`delivered [2206]`) with
  **9 `digest_page`** stored; the next run sent `{"posts":47,"images":3,"audioSec":57}`
  (`delivered [2207]`) with **33 new pages + 3 flood failures**, taking the stored count to **42 =
  9 kept + 33 new** — none of the 9 was published again. Both runs also show Telegraph's own ceiling:
  the first hit `FLOOD_WAIT_525` (a ~9-minute IP block earned by the earlier test batches), so a cold
  window can leave some "Also today" entries on their post URL until a later run.
- The cache filling up and then costing nothing, live: successive runs took the stored count
  **42 → 45 → 47** of the 47-post window, the last 3 pages and then the final 2 links arriving
  without a single flood wait; the run that started fully linked logged **0 `digest_page`, 0 waits,
  0 image failures**, `{"posts":47,"images":2,"audioSec":70}` (`delivered`), and the window report
  after it read `{"window":47,"linked":47,"unlinked":[]}`. Every run shipped pictures.
- The Instant View as the source, live (four runs over the same 47-post window): (a) no cache →
  **45 `digest_page`**, `images:1`, `{"delivered":[2202]}`; (b) every one of the 47 posts given its
  page, summaries cached → **0 `digest_page`**, `images:0` — the cache used to skip extraction;
  (c) same cache, summaries cleared so the articles are read again → **0 `digest_page`, 0 extract
  failures, 0 image failures, `images:1`**, audio 63 s, `{"delivered":[2204]}`, 0 rows left holding
  a link; (c) is the new path, the picture came through the Instant View copy since (b) proves the
  feed payload alone yields none. (d) with the cache-hit fix, the same cached state as (b) →
  `images:2`, 0 failures, `{"delivered":[2205]}`: a retry now ships the same pictures.
